title: token-lease-handshake-split-causing-brief-under-enforcement-and-unmetered-burst
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Symptom: a small subset of per-key requests (mostly high-traffic orgs hitting per-route burst windows) observed transient unthrottled bursts during shard handoff events. The burst correlated with node handoff windows when a lease was transferred between aggregator shards.

Observed behavior: metrics show a 30-120s spike in allowed requests for ~120 org-route keys during several scheduled shard rebalances. Billing dashboards reported higher token counts for affected orgs; tracing shows duplicate token allocation paths and a missing debit on the departing shard for the same logical token.

Why this is important: this can lead to short-lived overages (unmetered usage) and unreliable enforcement guarantees, violating SLOs and skewing billing reconciliation. We need a low-risk fix and thorough validation to avoid introducing new races during shard transitions.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-02: On-call alerted via SLO pager after automated checkers detected spike in per-route allowed QPS for shard-group eu-west-1-a.
2026-03-03: Reproduced locally with a sharded simulator. Rebalance scenario: shard A transfers lease for key K to shard B while in-flight tokens are being reconciled.

2026-03-04: Heap snapshots and logs show two code paths that can both emit a temporary allow: (1) target shard applying a reconstructed credit without seeing pending debit, (2) departing shard failing to finish commit due to socket timeout, leading to no final debit flush.

Root cause hypothesis: lease handshake uses two-phase messages (claim, ack) but message loss + concurrency allowed both shards to consider the same credit live for a short window. There is no monotonic sequence check on the token ledger, so duplicate allocation is possible.
We confirmed with trace IDs that some requests saw allowance decisions from both shards (fast path on B, stale permit on A) within 300ms of each other.
Customer reports: two mid-market customers reported unexpected hourly token spikes; both mapped to the same shard group and heavy per-route traffic pattern.
Related artifacts: cross-referenced with ENG-27458 (shard migration inconsistent metering) and ENG-214579 (shadowed retries skip meter incrementing).
root_cause: Non-atomic lease transfer + lack of monotonic ledger sequence led to temporary double-counting of available credits across shards. In-flight debits were not guaranteed to be persisted or reconciled before the target shard started allowing requests. The system relied on eventual reconciliation which is too slow for enforcement guarantees.
proposed_fix: Implement an idempotent ledger write with a monotonic 'transfer_epoch' and per-key sequence number embedded in every debit/credit entry.

Change the lease handshake to be a three-step: PREPARE (freeze outgoing debits for key), TRANSFER (commit epoch increment and atomically move outstanding delta), COMMIT (target shard publishes new epoch and starts serving). Use a quorum-safe commit for cloud control plane writes.

Add a short grace-window policy where the target shard returns 429 for ambiguous epoch stamps until it observes either the PREPARE completion or reconciler confirmation. Default grace-window: 500ms (configurable per deployment class).
Introduce a reconciliation step run immediately after TRANSFER that verifies outstanding in-flight debits on the departing node and applies compensating adjustments if necessary.
Backfill: run a one-off reconciliation job for the affected time ranges to correct billing for orgs with confirmed over-allow events.
Add unit and integration tests (simulated message loss, timeouts, and concurrent allows) and deterministic fuzz scenarios in the sharded simulator harness.
risk_analysis: Medium risk: changes touch the lease protocol and ledger commit path which are critical to enforcement correctness. Regression could cause under-enforcement (false throttles) if epoch logic is too strict.

Mitigations: feature-flag the new handshake, run canary rollout to 1 shard-group in staging, add automated back-pressure test to detect false positives, and keep fallback path that uses existing reconciliation for 60s if new path fails.
No customer-facing downtime expected; we will throttle more aggressively during ambiguous windows which is conservative from a billing perspective.

progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Prototype of transfer_epoch landed on a feature branch; basic unit tests added.
2026-03-07: Simulator reproduced race reliably with injected packet drops; confirmed PREPARE step prevents double-allow in prototype.
2026-03-09: Draft PR opened (see attachments). Security reviewed the plan and flagged KMS usage for ledger writes; follow-up to ensure secrets rotated properly.
2026-03-11: Integration tests flaked under heavy load in CI; increased timeout thresholds and made reconciler verification async with strong eventual consistency guarantees.
2026-03-12: Ready for initial canary in staging; planning verification dashboard and rollback playbook.
qa_plan: Deterministic simulator tests for packet loss, socket timeouts, and concurrent requests with epoch assertions.
Staging canary: enable feature-flag for single shard-group and run synthetic traffic that hits known edge patterns for 24h.
Monitor: per-route allow-rate, per-key ledger epoch mismatches, reconciliation counts, and billing deltas. Alert on any >0.5% unexpected allowance compared to baseline.
Manual validation: sample traces and token ledger entries for several keys before and after transfer.
rollout_steps: Canary to one shard-group in staging for 24h
Canary to 5% of production shard-groups with extended monitoring for 48h
Gradual ramp to 100% over a week if no anomalies
Run billing backfill job for confirmed affected time windows
Customer outreach to impacted accounts with remediation summary and credits if applicable
next_actions: Land PR and add required KMS key rotation step per security note
